options.text: Mixing different fractions of crude oil together
Breaking down long-chain hydrocarbons into shorter, more useful molecules
Joining small molecules together to make polymers

questions.explanation: Cracking is the process of breaking down long-chain hydrocarbons (which are in lower demand) into shorter-chain, more useful molecules such as petrol fractions and alkenes.

questions.stem: What are the two main types of cracking?
questions.explanation: The two main methods are steam cracking (using high temperature and steam) and catalytic cracking (using a zeolite catalyst at lower temperatures). Both break long chains into shorter ones.

questions.stem: What types of molecules are typically produced by cracking?
questions.explanation: Cracking produces a mixture of shorter alkanes (useful as fuels) and alkenes (useful for making polymers and other chemicals). At least one alkene is always produced.

options.text: It makes crude oil cheaper to extract
It converts less valuable long-chain fractions into more valuable shorter-chain products
It increases the amount of crude oil available
It reduces pollution from crude oil

questions.explanation: There is greater demand for shorter-chain products (like petrol) than long-chain ones (like heavy fuel oil). Cracking converts surplus long-chain molecules into the more valuable short-chain products.

questions.stem: Why are the alkenes produced by cracking particularly valuable?

options.text: They are used as food additives
They are used as monomers to make polymers (plastics) and as feedstock for other chemicals
They are used to make metals

questions.explanation: Alkenes from cracking are essential raw materials (feedstock) for the petrochemical industry. Ethene is used to make poly(ethene), ethanol, and many other chemicals.

questions.stem: In catalytic cracking, what catalyst is commonly used?
questions.explanation: Catalytic cracking uses a zeolite catalyst (made of aluminium oxide and silicon dioxide). The long-chain hydrocarbons are passed over the hot catalyst, which breaks them into smaller molecules.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a correct example of a cracking reaction?
questions.explanation: C₁₀H₂₂ → C₇H₁₆ + C₃H₆ shows a long-chain alkane (decane) being cracked into a shorter alkane (heptane) and an alkene (propene). The atoms are balanced on both sides.
